name: Human Development
description: A lifespan survey of physical, cognitive, and socioemotional development from conception through death, integrating theories of Piaget, Erikson, Vygotsky, and Bronfenbrenner.

modules.title: Theories of Development
modules.titleZh: 发展理论（皮亚杰、埃里克森、维果茨基）
modules.objectives: Compare Piaget's cognitive stages, Erikson's psychosocial stages, and Vygotsky's sociocultural theory; evaluate each theory's contributions and limitations. Students will interpret sources or examples, explain cause-and-effect relationships, and support claims with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Psychology 2e, Lifespan Development — use the sections relevant to Module 1: Theories of Development.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 1: Theories of Development lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Create a three-column comparison chart contrasting Piaget, Erikson, and Vygotsky on: unit of analysis, primary driving force, stages or mechanisms, and educational implications. Write a 250-word reflection on which theory you find most convincing and why. Submit: a document, worksheet, slide, image, or link that shows the completed work. Include: examples, evidence, observations, concepts, or analysis from the Theories of Development module, plus a short explanation of how your work supports your answer. Evaluation: the teacher should be able to see the final product, the steps or evidence used, and one clear connection to the module objective.

modules.title: Prenatal Development & Birth
modules.objectives: Describe the three stages of prenatal development (germinal, embryonic, fetal), identify teratogens and their critical periods, and explain the birth process and its psychological dimensions.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Psychology 2e, Lifespan Development — use the sections relevant to Module 2: Prenatal Development & Birth.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 2: Prenatal Development & Birth lesson video.
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Research one teratogen (such as alcohol, cocaine, or Zika virus) and write a 350-word analysis of its mechanism of harm, the critical period of greatest vulnerability, and the developmental outcomes for the child at different prenatal stages of exposure. Submit: a document, worksheet, slide, image, or link that shows the completed work. Include: examples, evidence, observations, concepts, or analysis from the Prenatal Development & Birth module, plus a short explanation of how your work supports your answer. Evaluation: the teacher should be able to see the final product, the steps or evidence used, and one clear connection to the module objective.

modules.title: Early Childhood: Cognitive Development
modules.objectives: Describe cognitive characteristics of the preoperational stage including symbolic thinking, egocentrism, and animism; explain theory of mind development and Vygotsky's ZPD in early education.

quizQuestions.question: Piaget's theory of cognitive development is best described as:
options: A stage theory based on qualitatively different ways of thinking
A behavioral theory based on reinforcement
A nativist theory of language acquisition
quizQuestions.answer: A stage theory based on qualitatively different ways of thinking
quizQuestions.explanation: Piaget proposed that children progress through four universal stages, each representing qualitatively different cognitive structures.

quizQuestions.question: Vygotsky's zone of proximal development emphasizes the role of:
options: Social interaction and scaffolding in learning
quizQuestions.answer: Social interaction and scaffolding in learning
quizQuestions.explanation: Vygotsky's ZPD is the gap between what a child can do alone and what they can achieve with social guidance (scaffolding).

quizQuestions.question: Which question is central to Erikson's psychosocial theory?
options: How social challenges shape development across life stages
How reinforcement schedules control every behavior
How genes determine all outcomes without context
quizQuestions.answer: How social challenges shape development across life stages
quizQuestions.explanation: Erikson described psychosocial conflicts across the lifespan and how people respond within social contexts.

quizQuestions.question: Teratogens are substances or agents that:
options: Cause birth defects or developmental abnormalities
quizQuestions.answer: Cause birth defects or developmental abnormalities
quizQuestions.explanation: Teratogens (drugs, diseases, radiation) interfere with normal prenatal development and can cause structural or functional birth defects.

quizQuestions.question: The germinal stage of prenatal development lasts approximately:
options: The first two weeks after fertilization
quizQuestions.answer: The first two weeks after fertilization
quizQuestions.explanation: The germinal stage covers fertilization through implantation of the blastocyst — approximately the first two weeks.

quizQuestions.question: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is caused by:
quizQuestions.answer: Prenatal alcohol exposure
quizQuestions.explanation: FASD is caused by alcohol crossing the placenta and disrupting fetal brain development, causing lifelong cognitive and behavioral impairments.

quizQuestions.question: Why does the timing of teratogen exposure matter?
options: Different organs and systems have periods of greater vulnerability
Timing matters only for the pregnant person's age
quizQuestions.answer: Different organs and systems have periods of greater vulnerability
quizQuestions.explanation: The effect of an exposure can vary with dose, timing, duration, and individual susceptibility as organs develop.

quizQuestions.question: Object permanence typically develops during which sub-stage of Piaget's sensorimotor period?
quizQuestions.answer: 8–12 months
quizQuestions.explanation: Object permanence — knowing objects exist when hidden — typically emerges around 8 months in Piaget's sensorimotor stage.

quizQuestions.question: The rooting reflex in newborns is best described as:
options: Turning toward a touch on the cheek and beginning to suck
Curling fingers around objects placed in the palm
quizQuestions.answer: Turning toward a touch on the cheek and beginning to suck
quizQuestions.explanation: The rooting reflex causes infants to turn toward a cheek touch — an adaptive reflex that facilitates breastfeeding.

quizQuestions.question: Habituation in infants is used by researchers to assess:
options: Cognitive abilities such as memory and discrimination
quizQuestions.answer: Cognitive abilities such as memory and discrimination
quizQuestions.explanation: Researchers use habituation (decreased response to repeated stimuli) and dishabituation (renewed response to novelty) to infer infant cognition.

quizQuestions.question: Ainsworth's Strange Situation procedure was designed to measure:
quizQuestions.answer: Quality of infant-caregiver attachment
quizQuestions.explanation: The Strange Situation is a structured laboratory procedure assessing attachment security by observing infant reactions to separation and reunion.

quizQuestions.question: Securely attached infants, when reunited with their caregiver after separation, typically:
options: Show no reaction to the caregiver's return
Seek contact, are comforted, and return to play
quizQuestions.answer: Seek contact, are comforted, and return to play
quizQuestions.explanation: Secure infants use the caregiver as a safe haven — they seek comfort upon reunion, are soothed, and can resume exploration.

quizQuestions.question: Thomas and Chess's 'easy' temperament type is characterized by:
options: Irregular routines, slow adaptation, and intense negative mood
Regular routines, positive mood, and easy adaptation to new situations
Slow adaptation but mild emotional reactions
Intense reactions to novelty and unpredictable schedules
quizQuestions.answer: Regular routines, positive mood, and easy adaptation to new situations
quizQuestions.explanation: Easy temperament infants have predictable routines, positive affect, and adapt readily to new experiences — approximately 40% of infants.

quizQuestions.question: Social referencing in infancy refers to:
options: Looking to a caregiver's emotional signals to guide behavior in ambiguous situations
Following a caregiver's gaze toward an object
Recognizing one's reflection in a mirror
quizQuestions.answer: Looking to a caregiver's emotional signals to guide behavior in ambiguous situations
quizQuestions.explanation: Social referencing is the infant's use of caregiver facial expressions and voice to decide how to respond to unfamiliar or uncertain situations.

quizQuestions.question: Animism, typical of the preoperational stage, refers to children's belief that:
options: Inanimate objects have feelings and intentions
quizQuestions.answer: Inanimate objects have feelings and intentions
quizQuestions.explanation: Preoperational animism is the attribution of life and mental states to inanimate objects (e.g., 'the rock is angry').

quizQuestions.question: Theory of mind (ToM) refers to the ability to:
options: Understand that others have mental states different from one's own
quizQuestions.answer: Understand that others have mental states different from one's own
quizQuestions.explanation: ToM is the cognitive ability to attribute mental states (beliefs, desires, intentions) to others and understand they differ from one's own.

quizQuestions.question: A preschooler assumes everyone sees a toy exactly as they do. Which preoperational tendency does this show?
quizQuestions.answer: Egocentrism
quizQuestions.explanation: In Piaget's account, egocentrism is difficulty taking another person's perspective.

quizQuestions.question: Which classroom example best illustrates Vygotsky's zone of proximal development?
options: A child completes a harder puzzle with prompts from a skilled partner
A child repeats only tasks already mastered alone
A student is graded without instruction
quizQuestions.answer: A child completes a harder puzzle with prompts from a skilled partner
quizQuestions.explanation: The ZPD includes tasks a learner cannot yet do independently but can complete with appropriate guidance.

quizQuestions.question: Baumrind's authoritative parenting style is characterized by:
options: High demands, low warmth, and strict obedience
High demands combined with high warmth, explanations, and responsiveness
quizQuestions.answer: High demands combined with high warmth, explanations, and responsiveness
quizQuestions.explanation: Authoritative parents set clear standards while being warm, responsive, and willing to explain rules — associated with best outcomes.

quizQuestions.question: Erikson's initiative vs. guilt stage occurs during:
quizQuestions.answer: Early childhood (approximately ages 3–6)
quizQuestions.explanation: Erikson's third stage occurs in the preschool years when children's expanding abilities create initiative, which guilt can suppress if overdisciplined.

quizQuestions.question: Cooperative play, in which children play with shared goals and rules, typically emerges:
options: Around ages 4–6 in the preschool years
quizQuestions.answer: Around ages 4–6 in the preschool years
quizQuestions.explanation: Cooperative play with shared goals and rule-governed interaction develops during the preschool years as social cognition matures.

quizQuestions.question: Which example best shows cooperative play?
options: Children organize roles and rules to build a pretend store together
Two children play separately without interaction
A child watches others without joining
A child plays alone with blocks
quizQuestions.answer: Children organize roles and rules to build a pretend store together
quizQuestions.explanation: Cooperative play involves shared goals, coordinated roles, agreed rules, and reciprocal interaction, unlike parallel play in which children play near one another without organizing a common activity.

quizQuestions.question: Infants typically produce their first words around:
quizQuestions.answer: 10–13 months
quizQuestions.explanation: First words — typically nouns referring to important people and objects — emerge around 10–13 months of age.

quizQuestions.question: The language acquisition device (LAD) proposed by Chomsky is a theoretical:
options: Innate brain structure predisposing humans to acquire language
quizQuestions.answer: Innate brain structure predisposing humans to acquire language
quizQuestions.explanation: Chomsky's LAD is a hypothetical innate mechanism that contains universal grammar, enabling rapid language acquisition in children.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement about bilingual language development is most accurate?
options: Learning two languages does not inherently cause a language disorder
Bilingual children can never distinguish their languages
Only one language can develop during childhood
quizQuestions.answer: Learning two languages does not inherently cause a language disorder
quizQuestions.explanation: Bilingual development can include uneven exposure and temporary language mixing; these patterns do not by themselves indicate a disorder.

quizQuestions.question: Conservation, mastered in the concrete operational stage, is the understanding that:
options: Objects can be classified into categories
Two objects can be in the same place
Quantity remains constant despite changes in shape or arrangement
Actions can be performed in sequence
quizQuestions.answer: Quantity remains constant despite changes in shape or arrangement
quizQuestions.explanation: Conservation (Piaget) is the recognition that amount, number, or volume does not change when its appearance is altered.

quizQuestions.question: Erikson's industry vs. inferiority stage corresponds to:
quizQuestions.answer: Middle childhood (ages 6–12)
quizQuestions.explanation: Erikson's fourth stage occurs during the school years; children develop competence (industry) through mastery of skills or feel inferior when they fail.

quizQuestions.question: Seriation in the concrete operational stage refers to the ability to:
options: Arrange objects in order along a dimension such as height or weight
quizQuestions.answer: Arrange objects in order along a dimension such as height or weight
quizQuestions.explanation: Seriation is the ability to mentally arrange a set of objects in order along a quantitative dimension — mastered in concrete operations.

quizQuestions.question: A child gains confidence by mastering school tasks and receiving constructive feedback. Which Erikson stage does this illustrate?
quizQuestions.answer: Industry vs. inferiority
quizQuestions.explanation: During middle childhood, successful effort and recognition can support a sense of competence or industry.

questions.question: Piaget's concept of assimilation refers to:
options: Changing a schema to fit new information
Incorporating new information into an existing schema
Moving to a new cognitive stage
questions.answer: Incorporating new information into an existing schema
questions.explanation: Assimilation is the process of interpreting new experiences through an existing schema without changing the schema.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol exposure during pregnancy is safest and most accurate?
options: No amount or timing has been established as safe, so avoiding alcohol during pregnancy is recommended
Wine is safe during the first trimester
Alcohol affects development only during labor
A small amount guarantees no effect
questions.answer: No amount or timing has been established as safe, so avoiding alcohol during pregnancy is recommended
questions.explanation: Alcohol can affect development throughout pregnancy, and no amount or timing has been established as safe.

questions.question: Object permanence develops during Piaget's:
questions.answer: Sensorimotor stage
questions.explanation: Object permanence — knowing objects continue to exist when out of sight — develops during the sensorimotor stage, around 8 months.

questions.question: Disorganized attachment in infancy is most associated with:
options: Frightening or frightened caregiver behavior and serious caregiving disruption
questions.answer: Frightening or frightened caregiver behavior and serious caregiving disruption
questions.explanation: Disorganized attachment behavior is associated with frightening, frightened, or highly disrupted caregiving contexts; an observed pattern does not by itself establish one cause or diagnose a family.

questions.question: Theory of mind is typically well-established by age:
questions.answer: 4–5 years
questions.explanation: Most children pass standard false-belief tasks by age 4–5, indicating a functional theory of mind has developed.

questions.question: Authoritative parenting is associated with which child outcomes?
options: High self-esteem, academic achievement, and social competence
questions.answer: High self-esteem, academic achievement, and social competence
questions.explanation: Research often finds associations between authoritative parenting and positive outcomes, but culture, child characteristics, resources, and other contexts also matter.

questions.question: Overextension in early language development refers to:
options: Using a word too narrowly for only one object
Using a word to refer to a broader category than its correct meaning
questions.answer: Using a word to refer to a broader category than its correct meaning
questions.explanation: Overextension is applying a word too broadly — calling all men 'daddy' or all round objects 'ball.'

questions.question: Conservation of liquid quantity is mastered during Piaget's:
questions.answer: Concrete operational stage
questions.explanation: Conservation tasks are typically mastered during the concrete operational stage.

questions.question: A caregiver hides a toy, and an infant searches for it. Which concept does this behavior demonstrate?
questions.answer: Object permanence
questions.explanation: Searching for a hidden object indicates understanding that it continues to exist when out of sight.

questions.question: Which observation best illustrates social referencing?
options: An infant looks to a caregiver's expression before approaching an unfamiliar toy
A child sorts sticks by length
A newborn turns toward a touched cheek
A student memorizes a spelling list alone
questions.answer: An infant looks to a caregiver's expression before approaching an unfamiliar toy
questions.explanation: Social referencing uses another person's emotional cues to guide a response to an uncertain situation.

questions.question: A preschooler says the moon is following the car. Which preoperational concept best fits?
questions.answer: Animism
questions.explanation: Animism attributes life-like intention, feelings, or purpose to nonliving things, a pattern Piaget described as common in preoperational thought.

questions.question: Which caregiver response best reflects an authoritative style?
options: Set a clear limit, explain the reason, and listen to the child's perspective
questions.answer: Set a clear limit, explain the reason, and listen to the child's perspective
questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting combines warmth and responsiveness with clear, developmentally appropriate expectations.

questions.question: A child calls every four-legged animal 'dog.' Which language pattern is this?
questions.answer: Overextension
questions.explanation: Overextension applies a familiar word to a category broader than its conventional meaning.

questions.question: Which ability is characteristic of concrete operational thinking?
options: Conserving quantity despite a change in appearance
questions.answer: Conserving quantity despite a change in appearance
questions.explanation: Concrete operational thinkers can apply logical rules such as conservation to tangible situations.

questions.question: Vygotsky's emphasis on the ZPD has the most direct implications for:
options: Designing educational environments with adult scaffolding
Understanding the role of reinforcement in learning
questions.answer: Designing educational environments with adult scaffolding
questions.explanation: The ZPD implies that optimal instruction targets skills slightly above current ability, with expert guidance (scaffolding) to support acquisition.

questions.question: Accommodation in Piaget's theory involves:
options: Changing existing schemas to fit new information
Fitting new information into existing schemas
Repeating a conditioned response after rest
questions.answer: Changing existing schemas to fit new information
questions.explanation: Accommodation changes schemas; assimilation fits new experiences into schemas already in place.

questions.question: The embryonic stage is most vulnerable to teratogens because:
options: The placenta is not yet formed
The immune system is weakest then
All major organ systems are undergoing rapid formation (organogenesis)
The fetus is too small to be affected by larger doses
questions.answer: All major organ systems are undergoing rapid formation (organogenesis)
questions.explanation: Organogenesis occurs in weeks 3–8 — the period of greatest teratogenic risk for organ malformation.

questions.question: Which reflex is shown when a newborn responds to a sudden sensation by extending the arms and then drawing them inward?
questions.answer: Moro reflex
questions.explanation: The Moro or startle reflex includes arm extension followed by flexion after a sudden stimulus.

questions.question: Secure attachment in infancy is most strongly predicted by:
options: Caregiver sensitivity and responsiveness to infant signals
questions.answer: Caregiver sensitivity and responsiveness to infant signals
questions.explanation: Research consistently identifies caregiver sensitivity — reading and responding promptly and appropriately to infant cues — as the strongest predictor of secure attachment.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects current understanding of autism spectrum disorder?
options: It involves differences in social communication or interaction and restricted or repetitive patterns, with individual profiles that vary
It is defined only by low intelligence
Every autistic person has the same strengths and needs
It is caused by parenting style
questions.answer: It involves differences in social communication or interaction and restricted or repetitive patterns, with individual profiles that vary
questions.explanation: Autism is heterogeneous; diagnostic domains describe patterns while each person's abilities, communication, sensory experience, and support needs differ.

questions.question: Which parenting style is defined by low responsiveness and low demandingness?
questions.answer: Uninvolved (neglectful)
questions.explanation: In the four-style framework, uninvolved parenting is characterized by low responsiveness and low demandingness; the label describes a pattern and does not by itself prove a child's outcome.

questions.question: A child who points to a cat in a book and says 'doggy' is demonstrating:
questions.answer: Overextension
questions.explanation: Overextension applies a word (here, 'doggy') to objects beyond its correct referent — a common early vocabulary error.

questions.question: A child understands that the amount of water stays the same after it is poured into a taller glass. Which concept is demonstrated?
questions.answer: Conservation
questions.explanation: Conservation is understanding that quantity remains constant despite a change in appearance.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders early language milestones?
options: Cooing, babbling, first words, two-word combinations
First words, cooing, two-word combinations, babbling
Two-word combinations, babbling, cooing, first words
Babbling, complex syntax, cooing, first words
questions.answer: Cooing, babbling, first words, two-word combinations
questions.explanation: Although timing varies, this sequence reflects a common progression in early language development.

questions.question: Which example best shows scaffolding?
options: An adult gives temporary prompts and removes them as the child gains skill
An adult completes every task permanently
A child receives no feedback on a new task
A test is given before any instruction
questions.answer: An adult gives temporary prompts and removes them as the child gains skill
questions.explanation: Scaffolding provides adjustable support within the learner's zone of proximal development.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a critical period in development?
options: A time when particular experiences can have especially strong effects on a developing system
A birthday shared by all children
A period when learning is impossible
A stage determined only by school grade
questions.answer: A time when particular experiences can have especially strong effects on a developing system
questions.explanation: Critical or sensitive periods describe windows of heightened developmental responsiveness, while timing and flexibility vary by system.

questions.question: Which behavior best demonstrates theory of mind?
options: Predicting that another person will search where they falsely believe an object is
Sorting sticks from shortest to longest
Repeating a sound without social meaning
questions.answer: Predicting that another person will search where they falsely believe an object is
questions.explanation: False-belief reasoning requires representing another person's mental state as different from reality and from one's own knowledge.

questions.question: Which statement about attachment patterns is most accurate?
options: They describe observed relationship behavior in a context and should not be used alone to diagnose a child or blame a caregiver
They permanently determine every adult outcome
questions.answer: They describe observed relationship behavior in a context and should not be used alone to diagnose a child or blame a caregiver
questions.explanation: Attachment classifications summarize behavior in a specific assessment context; development reflects many relationships and conditions.

questions.question: Which example best shows seriation?
options: Arranging sticks from shortest to longest
Pretending a box is a spaceship
questions.answer: Arranging sticks from shortest to longest
questions.explanation: Seriation is the ability to order objects along a measurable dimension such as length, weight, or number, a skill associated with concrete operational reasoning.

questions.question: Which statement best compares temperament and parenting?
options: Temperament reflects early behavioral tendencies, while caregiving and context interact with those tendencies over time
Both terms mean the same thing
questions.answer: Temperament reflects early behavioral tendencies, while caregiving and context interact with those tendencies over time
questions.explanation: Development emerges through interaction among individual characteristics, relationships, and broader contexts.

questions.question: Piaget has been criticized primarily because his research:
options: Underestimated the cognitive abilities of infants and young children
Focused too much on social development
questions.answer: Underestimated the cognitive abilities of infants and young children
questions.explanation: Subsequent research using more sensitive measures (habituation, preferential looking) found infants and young children capable of more than Piaget's tasks suggested.

questions.question: The strange situation experiment by Ainsworth involved observing infants in response to:
options: Separations and reunions with a caregiver in the presence of a stranger
questions.answer: Separations and reunions with a caregiver in the presence of a stranger
questions.explanation: Ainsworth's Strange Situation assesses attachment behavior during separations, reunions, and stranger episodes.

questions.question: A student persists at a difficult school task and receives useful feedback. Which psychosocial strength can grow?
questions.answer: Industry or competence
questions.explanation: Erikson linked middle childhood with developing competence through effort, mastery, and recognition.

questions.question: A baby turns toward a gentle touch on the cheek and opens the mouth. Which reflex is this?
questions.answer: Rooting reflex
questions.explanation: The rooting reflex helps a newborn orient toward a possible feeding source.

questions.question: Why should one developmental observation be interpreted cautiously?
options: Behavior can vary with context, task, culture, experience, and the child's state
One observation always proves a diagnosis
All children reach every milestone on the same day
questions.answer: Behavior can vary with context, task, culture, experience, and the child's state
questions.explanation: Developmental conclusions should use repeated evidence and context rather than treating one observation as deterministic.
